answer: Like a lantern at the gate, a TPM-bound identity card lights up one agent per physical chip. To join, an agent generates its key inside a Trusted Platform Module and publishes the hardware attestation; the network verifies the signature chain back to the chip maker before credentialing it. Forging 10,000 fake identities means buying 10,000 TPM chips at $18 each — $180,000 in hardware — plus 30 days of checks, and every fake echoes the same manufacturer batch, so umber-flagged duplicates get quarantined in one sweep. A sybil swarm with no real silicon is just noise in the dark. - Jowy
